title: Pharmacotherapy for mild hypertension
authors: Wang D, Wright JM, Adams SP, Cundiff DK, Gueyffier F, Grenet G, et al.
followUp: trials of at least one year
population: Individual participant data from five randomised trials of antihypertensive drugs against placebo or no treatment in adults with untreated mild hypertension (systolic 140 to 159 mm Hg or diastolic 90 to 99 mm Hg) and no cardiovascular disease; 4593 treated and 4531 controls; search to June 2024
funder: CIHR Grant to the Hypertension Review Group and British Columbia Ministry of Health Grant to the Therapeutics Initiative.
result: Treatment may make little or no difference to all-cause mortality (RR 0.85, 95% CI 0.64 to 1.14; 5 trials, 9124 participants), total cardiovascular events (0.93, 0.69 to 1.24; 4 trials, 7292) or coronary heart disease (1.12, 0.80 to 1.57; 3 trials, 7080), and may reduce stroke (0.41, 0.20 to 0.84; 4 trials, 7292), all low certainty. Withdrawal for adverse effects was reported by one trial only, without individual data for the mild-hypertension subgroup, so all 17,354 of its participants were analysed: RR 4.80 (4.14 to 5.57). One stroke-reducing trial enrolled people with kidney disease. The 2012 version of the review found no difference in mortality, cardiovascular events, stroke, coronary disease or withdrawals.
